# featbit_policy (Resource)

Manages one custom FeatBit Policy and its complete statement set through the documented public API.

This resource manages only `CustomerManaged` Policies. Use the
`featbit_policy` data source to observe a built-in `SysManaged` Policy; no
resource lifecycle can mutate or delete one.

`statements` is the complete unordered statement set. Terraform replaces the
server's complete set when it changes, including when it is configured as
empty. Statement order, action order, resource order, and tag order are
canonicalized and do not create meaningful drift.

## Required parent access

Feature Flag or Segment actions do not by themselves grant visibility into
their parent Project and Environment. Grant the appropriate
`CanAccessProject` and `CanAccessEnv` statements alongside leaf permissions,
as the example does. This is required for a Member to navigate to and use the
authorized leaf objects.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "project_key" {
  description = "Organization-scoped, case-sensitive exact Project key."
  type        = string
}

variable "environment_key" {
  description = "Case-sensitive exact Environment key within the selected Project."
  type        = string
}

data "featbit_project" "target" {
  key = var.project_key
}

data "featbit_environment" "target" {
  project_id = data.featbit_project.target.id
  key        = var.environment_key
}

resource "featbit_policy" "developer" {
  name        = "Checkout developers"
  key         = "checkout-developers"
  description = "Parent visibility plus scoped Flag and Segment operations"

  statements = [
    {
      resource_type = "project"
      effect        = "allow"
      actions       = ["CanAccessProject"]
      resources     = ["project/${data.featbit_project.target.key}"]
    },
    {
      resource_type = "env"
      effect        = "allow"
      actions       = ["CanAccessEnv"]
      resources     = ["project/${data.featbit_project.target.key}:env/${data.featbit_environment.target.key}"]
    },
    {
      resource_type = "flag"
      effect        = "allow"
      actions       = ["ToggleFlag", "UpdateFlagName"]
      resources     = ["project/${data.featbit_project.target.key}:env/${data.featbit_environment.target.key}:flag/*"]
    },
    {
      resource_type = "segment"
      effect        = "allow"
      actions       = ["UpdateSegmentDescription", "UpdateSegmentRules"]
      resources     = ["project/${data.featbit_project.target.key}:env/${data.featbit_environment.target.key}:segment/*"]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Statement catalog

`resource_type` and `effect` are exact lower-case values. The supported
effects are `allow` and `deny`. Actions are exact and case-sensitive:

| `resource_type` | Supported actions |
|---|---|
| `project` | `CanAccessProject`, `CreateProject`, `DeleteProject`, `UpdateProjectSettings`, `CreateEnv` |
| `env` | `CanAccessEnv`, `DeleteEnv`, `UpdateEnvSettings`, `DeleteEnvSecret`, `CreateEnvSecret`, `UpdateEnvSecret` |
| `flag` | `*`, `CreateFlag`, `ArchiveFlag`, `RestoreFlag`, `DeleteFlag`, `CloneFlag`, `CopyFlagTo`, `ToggleFlag`, `UpdateFlagName`, `UpdateFlagDescription`, `UpdateFlagOffVariation`, `UpdateFlagVariations`, `UpdateFlagTags`, `UpdateFlagDefaultRule`, `UpdateFlagIndividualTargeting`, `UpdateFlagTargetingRules` |
| `segment` | `*`, `CreateSegment`, `ArchiveSegment`, `RestoreSegment`, `DeleteSegment`, `UpdateSegmentName`, `UpdateSegmentDescription`, `UpdateSegmentTags`, `UpdateSegmentTargetingUsers`, `UpdateSegmentRules` |

The action `*` is supported only for `flag` and `segment` statements.

Resource selectors must preserve the full hierarchy for their control level:

| `resource_type` | Selector form |
|---|---|
| `project` | `project/<project_key>` |
| `env` | `project/<project_key>:env/<environment_key>` |
| `flag` | `project/<project_key>:env/<environment_key>:flag/<flag_key>[;<tag>[,<tag>...]]` |
| `segment` | `project/<project_key>:env/<environment_key>:segment/<segment_key>[;<tag>[,<tag>...]]` |

Each key position can be one exact case-sensitive key or the whole-token
wildcard `*`. A global `*`, partial glob, incomplete hierarchy, whitespace,
or reserved selector delimiters inside a key or tag are invalid. Tag suffixes
are available only on Flag and Segment selectors and use OR semantics.

## Lifecycle

- `name`, `description`, and the complete statement set update in place.
- `key` is organization-scoped exact identity and requires replacement.
- Create refuses an existing exact key rather than adopting it automatically.
- Destroy refuses while any exact Group or direct-Member association remains.
  Remove those bindings first.
- Mutations execute once and are followed by exact reads. Confirmed
  intermediate state is retained if a multi-call operation partially fails.

## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Immutable organization-scoped exact Policy key.
- `name` (String) Policy display name.
- `statements` (Attributes Set) Complete unordered Policy statement set. An empty set removes every statement. Statement actions and selectors are validated against the managed IAM v1 catalog. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--statements))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Policy description. An omitted value canonicalizes to an empty string.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Policy UUID.
- `type` (String) Policy ownership type. Managed resources are always CustomerManaged.

<a id="nestedatt--statements"></a>
### Nested Schema for `statements`

Required:

- `actions` (Set of String) Non-empty set of exact case-sensitive actions valid for resource_type.
- `effect` (String) Exact lowercase effect: allow or deny.
- `resource_type` (String) Exact lowercase control level: project, env, flag, or segment.
- `resources` (Set of String) Non-empty set of wildcard or exact-key selectors matching resource_type.

## Import

Import one custom Policy with its UUID:

```shell
terraform import featbit_policy.developer '<policy_uuid>'
```

The identifier must use 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal UUID form. Importing a built-in
Policy into this resource is rejected before any mutation; observe it with the
data source instead.
